review.verdict: Casting and color are solid, but clipped elements at the frame edges, an underfilled right half with an uneven gap, a near-illegible blank rulebook, and a vertical-divider-plus-tag-label composition that's been used twice recently pull the average below the bar.
revisionNotes: Robot and teen2 clip the safe area (lint-flagged): scale robot down to ~1.0 or shift x 0.17→0.21; shift teen2 to x~0.84 so the right arm stops clipping at the frame edge.

Composition is lopsided in both halves — left mass (robot+diplomat+label) crowds x 0.17-0.4 leaving the center empty, and the right half has a dead gap between the divider and the eye-bag; pull eye-bag to x~0.56 and spread teens to fill the half.
Brief calls for 'a cluster of diplomats' but only one sitting figure appears, reading as one shrugging person rather than a stalled summit — add a second seated human at the table.
The table/open-rulebook prop reads as a small stool with a tiny tag at this scale; bump table scale to ~1.3 and keep the paper rect clearly white so 'blank rulebook' is legible.
'FALSE ALARM' label straddles the vertical divider line, visually crossing into the left half; reposition it (or change attach side) so it sits fully inside the right half.
The siren above teen2 reads as a beret/hat, not a flashing police light; enlarge the red/blue domes and add a flash mark so it's unmistakably a siren.

Composition device (vertical-divider split frame with two short tag labels) repeats at least two recent sloppers ('CHIEF RESIGNS/RIVAL LAUNCHES', 'PAUSED/TWICE AS FAST') — try a different split device or a single unified scene for freshness.

review.verdict: The cast and metaphor are sound, but the left scene is a tangled overlap of robot/diplomats/table and the right scene is missing its key prop (the bag), so the joke doesn't read cleanly in 3 seconds — not ready to publish.
revisionNotes: The robot, table, and both diplomats are anchored almost on top of each other (x 0.2/0.3/0.39, same y) — pull the robot back to a background anchor (x 0.15, y 0.55, scale 1.3) so it looms behind without its arms/torso colliding with the diplomats' bodies.

The bag of chips is missing from the render — it's the whole point of the right-hand joke. Give it its own visible raw-shape component (rounded rectangle, a few horizontal snack-bag lines) at the base of the camera pole, scaled ~0.4, clearly separate from the pole's foot.
The open rulebook is swallowed inside the diplomats' chests — raise the table/paper anchor or shrink diplomat scale slightly so the blank page is visible above their laps.
No thin vertical divider line between the two halves as specified in the brief — add it to separate 'no rules' from 'false alarm' and tighten the composition.
The siren/flashing-light raw shape (two overlapping half-domes) doesn't read as a police light; redraw with a clear dome plus flash rays or swap for a simpler recognizable shape.
Left half is crowded and tangled while the right half floats in empty space — rebalance by spreading the camera/bag/teens/siren group wider or bumping teen scale to ~0.7.

Teen2 is clipped at the right safe-area edge (x845-1056); move its anchor left to x=0.84 and reduce scale to 0.65 so both teens are fully inside the frame.

The bag is nearly invisible at scale 0.4; bump it to ~0.9 and move it directly beneath the camera-pole (e.g. x=0.63, y=0.83) so the AI-eye's downward gaze and the bag read as one connected beat instead of two unrelated props.
The siren floats in empty space between the divider and the teens with no visual link to them; move its anchor closer to the teens (x≈0.8, y≈0.6) and ground its pole on the sidewalk line.
The 'NO RULES' label sits directly over the diplomats' faces/book; reattach it to the side of the table instead of on top to avoid overlapping the cast.
